oracle_price_stale_at_creation.meaning: the pull-based oracle price is stale (lagging) at the time a market is created
oracle_price_stale_at_creation.checkpoint: before market creation reads the oracle price

creation_oracle_update_consistent.meaning: market creation updates the oracle consistently with post-creation user flows (mint/redeem/swap) that update the oracle first

post_creation_flow_updates_oracle_first.meaning: post-creation user flows (mint/redeem/swap) update the oracle first

arbitrage_price_gap_realized.meaning: an attacker creates a market when the oracle lags, then immediately performs mint/redeem/swap (which refreshes to the true price) to arbitrage the price gap established at initialization
arbitrage_price_gap_realized.checkpoint: after market creation and immediate post-creation mint/redeem/swap

assumptions: The report treats 'consistent with post-creation user flows' as the oracle being updated before the price is read, matching the contrast in evidence e_41ff6b99b3df_0011.

unresolved.description: The intent states a consistency requirement between market creation and post-creation flows but does not give a numeric or field-level definition of 'consistent'; the correspondence is encoded with grounded Boolean observables and requires code-level binding.

limitations: The impact is potential; the impact_outcome Boolean records the reported arbitrage scenario rather than asserting it as inevitable.
The correspondence pattern equates the creation-time oracle update behavior with the post-creation flow behavior; the report does not supply a numeric price or field value to compare.

links.reported_relation: createMarket forwards to initMarket without updating the oracle, so a stale price is used at initialization.
Post-creation flows update the oracle first, so an immediate mint/redeem/swap refreshes to the correct price and unlocks arbitrage of the mispricing.
initMarket reads the price immediately without updating the oracle, so a stale price makes the market born mispriced.
